To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the C terminus of c-Fos is required for serum-induced DNA synthesis, and the Fos protein is not interchangeable with Jun or v-Fos.

the c-fos antisense RNA is able to inhibit the expression of the endogenous Fos protein, that antisense-resistant Fos mutants are able to restore serum-induced DNA-synthesis to anti-fos-expressing cells, that FBR v-foss protein is unable to restore serum-induced proliferation to anti-fos RNA-expressing cells and that overexpression of Jun is unable to restore the ability of serum-induced proliferation to these cells.

(1) the C-terminal domain of c-Fos protein is required for rescue of c-Fos expression and serum-induced DNA synthesis, (2) c-Fos and c-Jun proteins have different functions, and (3) c-Fos protein has a specialized function in serum-induced DNA synthesis which cannot be replaced by FBR v-FOS or c-Jun proteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role that c-fos plays in the control of cell growth and differentiation.
the identification of functional domains of c-Fos protein and their role in the regulation of gene expression and cellular proliferation.
understanding the mechanisms by which cells control the expression of genes encoding proteins that regulate the cell cycle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the C terminus of Fos is essential for its specialized function in the induction of DNA synthesis by serum.
the Fos protein is required for serum-induced DNA synthesis and that the C terminus is necessary for the function of Fos.
the C-terminal domain of c-Fos protein is essential for serum-induced DNA synthesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
c-Fos protein plays a specialized role in serum-induced DNA synthesis and that this role requires the C-terminal 50 amino acids.
the c-Fos protein has a specialized function in addition to the generalized function(s) of the AP-1 complex.
c-Fos protein is required for serum-induced DNA synthesis but not for serum-induced expression of c-jun mRNA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the FBR v-fs protein is not able to rescue the serum-induced DNA synthesis, and the FBR v-FOS is not able to transactivate the AP-1 target genes.

the FBR v-FOS protein is not equivalent to c-FOS in its ability to rescue the effects of anti-fos RNA on serum-induced DNA synthesis, and that c-Jun is not equivalent to FOS in the ability to rescue the effect of anti-fos expression.
c-Fos and c-Jun proteins are not interchangeable in the serum induction of DNA synthesis.
